exposure: delivery-specific healthcare professional-related health control beliefs
outcome: preference for spontaneous vaginal birth in hospital
general preference index for medicalized ways of delivery
cohort: The study included 984 Hungarian nulliparous women (mean age 26.45 years), consisting of 660 non-pregnant and 224 pregnant individuals.
finding: Healthcare professional-related control beliefs were associated with a stronger preference for spontaneous vaginal birth in hospital and planned cesarean birth, and a weaker preference for home birth, while internal delivery-specific control beliefs predicted a weaker preference for planned cesarean and a stronger preference for home birth.
mod_finding: Delivery-specific control beliefs were significantly associated with preferences for spontaneous vaginal birth in hospital, planned cesarean birth, and home birth.
